clue.text: Large flat round burger — ultimately good North American food

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the large flat goes about the next piece

parts.note: a condo is a North American word for a large apartment, or flat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word burger

explanation.surface: Someone praises a big, flat, circular hamburger as the best food America has to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts R, the last letter of 'burger' ('ultimately'), inside CONDO, then G follows. 'Burger' looks like part of the food, but it only gives its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn dog is a sausage coated in cornmeal batter and fried, a classic American fairground snack.

clue.text: Herb taking North American food, gobbling horse up

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing, so the food holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: an Oreo is the famous American chocolate sandwich biscuit

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word horse is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: A herb is described as eating American food while consuming a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the horse because this is a down clue; the result sits after the first three letters of the biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a Mediterranean culinary herb of the marjoram family, used on pizza.

clue.text: North American food, bit chipped off?

definitions.text: North American food, bit chipped off?

indicators.note: a bit chipped off means a small part of the word for food is lost, here its final letter

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: A piece of American food seems to have a chip missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: as wordplay, NA plus CHOW with a letter knocked off; as definition, a nacho is a tortilla chip, a little bit of food that is literally a chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, often topped with cheese, from Tex-Mex cooking.

clue.text: Cricketers back in the pavilion, or in the field, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the batting team that has been dismissed is the side that is out, back in the pavilion
being in a field is being in the open air, not indoors

explanation.surface: A question about where a cricket team is, either back in the clubhouse or out on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the PAVILION is the clubhouse where batters who are out sit; the team that is out is read as OUT SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is the team that has been dismissed; as one word it means in the open air.

clue.text: See 23
Hash is on my right, North American food

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a plate of hash is sitting on their right, an American dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hash' looks like the food itself, but it is the instruction to rearrange 'is on my right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hominy grits are coarsely ground dried maize kernels, boiled into a porridge eaten in the American South.

clue.text: Island with something black, another colour featured prominently as well

parts.note: Cos, also spelt Kos, is a Greek island in the Aegean
tar is a thick black substance
red is a colour, another one after black

explanation.surface: A description of an island painted in black and another colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured prominently as well' means shared top billing with another actor.
explanation.definitionFit: To share star billing in a film or play is to appear as one of its leading performers alongside another.

clue.text: Cut up Paul's check

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for cut is read upwards

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it
Paul is the setter, so the setter's means belonging to me

explanation.surface: Paul asks someone to cut up his cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA. 'Paul's' is the setter speaking: what is Paul's is MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to inspect or scrutinise it closely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Many captivated by new image, plan for English town

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside, so the many sit within the rearranged words
new signals that the following words are made into something different

parts.note: tons is informal for many, a great number

explanation.surface: A town's planners show off a fresh image that has won over many people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'many' sit between the two halves of the rearranged letters. Royal Leamington Spa is a Warwickshire spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Leamington Spa is a spa town in Warwickshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: "Danke" translated almost as "German vehicle"

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, its last letter missing

parts.note: Danke is German for thank you; translated into French it becomes merci

explanation.surface: A German thank-you is being rendered as the name of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danke' is German for thanks; in French the word is MERCI, and 'almost' takes off the final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is the informal British shortening of Mercedes, the German car marque.

clue.text: That which controls temperature by a few switches about right?

definitions.text: That which controls temperature by a few switches about right?

indicators.note: by is read loosely as held on either side, so the word that wraps the rest; the question mark excuses the licence
about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the right
switches means turns over, so the few is read backwards

parts.note: some means a few, an unspecified small number

explanation.surface: A device that regulates heat by flicking a few switches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' and 'temperature' each work twice: in the definition and in the wordplay, which the question mark flags. 'switches' reverses SOME to EMOS; 'about' puts it around R, and T follows before THAT wraps it all.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat is the device that keeps a heating system at a set temperature, switching it on and off.

clue.text: Swan in prison, no finale for Shakespearean actor

indicators.note: in means the swan is placed inside the shortened prison
no finale means the prison word loses its last letter

parts.note: jail is a prison
a cob is a male swan

explanation.surface: A swan is locked up in jail, a story with no ending about an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan' suggests the bird or a verb, but here it is the male bird's name. Sir Derek Jacobi is famed for Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Derek Jacobi is an English actor famed for his Shakespearean stage roles.

clue.text: Chinese food

definitions.meaning: the standard Chinese language of Beijing
a small loose-skinned orange, a fruit

explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is both the main Chinese language and a kind of citrus fruit, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Cheap rope, funny in knots

indicators.note: rope that is in knots is tangled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some cheap rope has got itself tied in comical knots.
explanation.walkthrough: FOURPENNY is old British money: something costing four old pence was cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Fourpenny describes something costing four old pence, hence of little value or inexpensive.

clue.text: Tenant wanted agent to include Turkish capital in search

indicators.note: in means the agent piece is placed inside the search word

parts.note: to root is to search, as in rooting around

indicators.note: to include means the agent holds the capital letter within it

parts.note: a mole is a spy, an agent planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word Turkish

explanation.surface: An estate agent is looking in Ankara for someone to rent a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkish capital' suggests Ankara, but it is just the first letter of Turkish. The letter goes after the first letter of the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign reading room to let advertises a room for rent, so it says a tenant is wanted.

clue.text: See 23
Baby son on show

parts.note: prog is short for programme, a television show

explanation.surface: A baby boy appears on a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: SPROG is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is informal British slang for a baby or young child.

clue.text: Language unit — I await your call?

definitions.meaning: a distinct unit of sound in a language
a request to be rung up

explanation.definitionFit: A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound in linguistics; split in two, it asks someone to ring.

clue.text: Personnel not quite catching on, journalist incapable in the end, picking nothing up?

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the shortened staff word surrounds the rest
not quite means the staff word loses its last letter

parts.note: staff are the personnel of an organisation
ED, short for editor, is a common crossword journalist

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word incapable

explanation.surface: Staff barely notice a hopeless journalist who seems to be picking up nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking nothing up' is the definition: a deaf person hears no sound. The final E comes from 'incapable' ('in the end').
explanation.definitionFit: Someone completely deaf hears no sound at all, so they pick up nothing.

clue.text: Certainly not confirmed as most imperial

parts.note: no is a firm refusal, certainly not
blest, an old form of blessed, describes someone received into the church

explanation.surface: Someone denies that the grandest figure has been confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblest means most grand and stately, the superlative of a regal, dignified quality.

clue.text: Quickly found an expert like Fred Astaire?

parts.note: Fred Astaire was a celebrated tap dancer
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Someone finds an expert dancer in the mould of Fred Astaire.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire really was A TAP ACE, which gives the clue its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a pace means doing it fast, at speed.

clue.text: Frog's uphill walk about 880 yards?

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, so the definition is simply a frog

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed walk goes around the distance
uphill in a down clue means the word walk is read upwards

parts.note: a trek is a long walk
880 yards is half a mile, and half of the word mile is MI

explanation.surface: A frog sets off on a long uphill walk of about half a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uphill' turns TREK into KERT in this down clue. 880 yards is half a mile, and MI is also half the letters of the word mile.
explanation.definitionFit: Kermit is the famous Muppet frog created by Jim Henson.

clue.text: Here crunchiest kind of battered North American food

indicators.note: battered means beaten about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: This is the crunchiest sort of American dish coated in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' looks like a description of the food, which it also is, but it is the signal to rearrange all the preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Southern fried chicken is chicken pieces coated in seasoned flour or batter and deep-fried, from the American South.

clue.text: Writer munching food so unnatural? A North American food

indicators.note: munching means eating, so the pen holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer
GM stands for genetically modified, food altered unnaturally

explanation.surface: A writer is eating genetically altered food and finds it a very American meal.
explanation.walkthrough: GM food is genetically modified food, hence 'so unnatural?'. Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Big Mac is McDonald's signature double-decker hamburger.

clue.text: See 6
Rejecting dog, gourmet after milky mixture including eggs for a start, as North American food

indicators.note: after means the gourmet piece comes behind the milky piece
including means the shuffled letters hold the egg letter within them
a mixture is a mingling, so these letters are rearranged
for a start means the first letter of the word eggs
rejecting means throwing out, so the dog is taken from the gourmet

parts.note: an epicure is a gourmet, a lover of fine food
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A gourmet turns down a dog and makes a creamy mix with eggs, an American dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges the milky letters into KYLIM before the egg letter goes in; 'Rejecting' leaves EPIE. Key lime pie comes from the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Key lime pie is a Florida dessert of lime custard in a pastry or biscuit base.

clue.text: Nation formerly in my command?

parts.note: my, from the speaker's point of view, gives I
to command is to run things; formerly puts it in the past tense, ran

explanation.surface: A leader recalls a country once under their command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formerly' puts the verb in the past: I once had command, so I RAN it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Revolutionary, for example, with report to carry

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the example abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: to state is to report

explanation.surface: A revolutionary, for instance, files a report to be carried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel; it turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gestate is to carry young in the womb during pregnancy.

clue.text: Virtuous type has a drop hidden away

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a virtuous person
to shed is to drop, as trees shed leaves

explanation.surface: A good person has a drink stowed away out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a drop' looks like a drink, but 'drop' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stashed has been stored secretly, put somewhere out of sight.
